description:
The palace at Pakoszów stands in the Jelenia Góra basin, long known for its linen trade. According to the European Route of Castles and Palaces it was raised in 1725 at the initiative of Johann Martin Gottfried, mayor of Jelenia Góra, on a rectangular plan with a mansard roof; another source gives 1720.

Frederick II, king of Prussia, is said to have stayed in the palace three times. From 1771 it belonged to Heinrich Hess, a merchant and director of a sugar refinery in Jelenia Góra. Besides serving as a residence, it was used as a linen-bleaching works after Frederick II granted a water privilege in 1777 allowing the use of water from the nearby Kamienna river, and it came to be called the Hess Bleaching Factory.

After many years of neglect, the building was bought by the grandson of the last pre-war owner, and it now houses a five-star hotel with a restaurant, an indoor swimming pool and a wellness area. The palace can be visited with a guide after prior reservation.
history: The palace at Pakoszów (German: Schloss Wernersdorf), today part of Piechowice, was raised in 1725 at the initiative of Johann Martin Gottfried, mayor of Jelenia Góra, according to the European Route of Castles and Palaces; another source gives 1720. It was built on a rectangular plan with a mansard roof, and Frederick II of Prussia is said to have stayed there three times. From 1771 the palace belonged to Heinrich Hess, a merchant and director of a sugar refinery in Jelenia Góra. Besides serving as a residence, it was used as a linen-bleaching works after Frederick II granted a water privilege in 1777 allowing the use of water from the nearby Kamienna river, and it came to be called the Hess Bleaching Factory. After many years of neglect and destruction, the building was bought by the grandson of the last pre-war owner, and it now houses a hotel and a restaurant.
